original.target_description: Original Experiment 2: Relationship between use of generic masculine language versus explicitly naming both sexes and the gender of people brought to mind.

notes: Identity checked independently from article title NAME YOUR FAVORITE MUSICIAN / Effects of Masculine Generics and of Their Alternatives in German, authors Dagmar Stahlberg, Sabine Sczesny, Friederike Braun, journal Vol. 20 No. 4 December 2001 pp. 464-469. These match the original reference. The DOI is not printed in the supplied text and was not independently resolved. Supplied candidate is an author-provided ResearchGate full-text HTML extraction, containing the article through notes and references, not merely an abstract; no PDF is supplied. Trailing book-review text is unrelated and excluded. All extraction concerns original Experiment 2; replication/pilot/extension qualifiers in some neutral descriptions do not change the assigned original-side primary study. Unassigned fields and replication/reported_success are placeholders. Target correspondence unresolved: Type-of-generic omnibus F(2,84)=9.97, p<.001; masculine versus pooled alternatives contrast p<.01; capital I versus masculine Scheffé p<.01; word pairs versus masculine Scheffé p>.10. No printed contrast effect sizes. No candidate is selected using row position or numeric matching. Whole primary Experiment 2 sample candidate: 45 female + 45 male = 90 participants, from explicitly disjoint sex groups; this is not assigned as row-specific analytic N. Four capital-I respondents were omitted only in a separately reported sensitivity analysis; no revised test statistics are printed.
